decision_rules_in_one_firestore_transact: StatCan reporting month NEWER than the stored month -> write (merge).
Same month, document already from the verified series -> NO write and NO audit-log entry (also not rewritten on repeat runs).
OLDER month than stored -> NO write: a missing or rolled-back release never overwrites a newer value.
Same month but stored from another series (the old unadjusted 14-10-0017-01 value) -> one corrective write, then stable.
Stored month unreadable -> write (repairs a malformed document).

StatCan unreachable, empty data, or the series identity check fails -> NO write; the stat document is never read or written and the Firestore handle is not even requested; one failure entry in data_audit_log.
scheduler_strategy.stored_month_is_read_from: latest_period (our documents), the engine's older "YYYY-MM" updated field, or a display label such as "Sep 2026".
deliberate_limits: A revision of the already-published latest month (same month, different value) is NOT rewritten; it is picked up with the next month's release, which refreshes the whole 12-month trend. This is the stated rule (only newer reporting periods update).
The manual canonical / live uploads are operator actions and do not apply the "only newer" gate (canonical also wipes the collection by design). They are protected only against stale saved files.
Operators who run the monthly tier by hand will no longer refresh Canada unemployment; they must run `npm run scheduler:ca-unemployment` after StatCan's release.

implementation.dry_run: Fetch + verify StatCan, read ONLY social_stats/CA_unemploymentRate, print existing vs proposed month/value and WRITE/SKIP. Performs no Firestore write, no audit-log write and creates no backup. A dry run never creates a failure audit entry. `--dry-run` is accepted ONLY as exactly `--ca-unemployment --dry-run`; in any other command form the scheduler refuses to start, so the flag can never be silently ignored while a real job runs. The cron registration always runs the real check and is unchanged.
implementation.project_guard: Before the first Firestore read the credential must be bound to civic-voice-5ea94 and no GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT / GCLOUD_PROJECT hint may differ (status PROJECT_MISMATCH: no read, write, backup or audit entry). The project id comes from the local credential object; no network is used to learn it.
implementation.pre_write_backup: When a write would REPLACE an existing document, its complete original contents are saved as JSON (document id/path, backup timestamp, firebase project, transaction attempt, type-tagged values) in a directory outside any git repository, inside the same transaction and BEFORE tx.set. Files are created exclusively (never overwritten), mode 0600, read back and verified, and refused if they contain service-account / private-key material. If the backup cannot be written and verified the transaction is abandoned and nothing is written (status BACKUP_FAILED). A first-ever write (no document) has nothing to preserve; skips and dry runs create no backup. Backups are not committed (outside the repository).

transaction_retry_review.question: Does the backup used for recovery represent the exact document version ultimately overwritten when Firestore retries the transaction?
transaction_retry_review.answer: YES for the committing attempt, with one reporting flaw that was fixed. Every retry re-runs the callback, re-reads the document and re-takes the backup; a commit succeeds only if the document is unchanged since that attempt's read, so the backup from the attempt that commits is the exact version that was replaced. The flaw: backups written by EARLIER attempts (versions that were never overwritten) stayed on disk indistinguishable from the real one and were not reported.
transaction_retry_review.fix: Each backup records transaction_attempt; the result reports attempts, the single recovery `backup`, and supersededBackups (after a write) or unusedBackups (skip / failed commit); the log names the one recovery point and warns not to restore the others. Nothing is deleted. A retry that finds the document gone reports no recovery point (stale reference cleared); a retry that finds a newer month skips and writes nothing.
transaction_retry_review.tests: 6 focused tests in test/ca-unemployment-dryrun-backup.test.js (retry sees a different version; several retries; retry finds a newer month; retry finds the document gone; commit fails after a backup; no-retry baseline) and 3 mutations proven caught.

implementation.audit_log: Unchanged. A successful update writes social_stats/CA_unemploymentRate (merge) plus ONE data_audit_log entry (scheduler_tier "ca_unemployment"); a failure writes one failure entry; skips and dry runs write none; PROJECT_MISMATCH writes none (it would go to the wrong project).
